llm.summary: This is a documentation-only hook-authoring guide with risky examples that are relevant to its purpose but should be copied carefully.

dimensions.detail: The skill teaches Claude Code and SDK hook authoring, including validation, logging, HTTP hooks, permission hooks, context injection, and persistent state; these capabilities are coherent with the stated purpose but can affect sensitive agent behavior if implemented broadly.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The guidance explains plugin, project, and global hook scopes and warns that global hooks run everywhere with the user's credentials, though some examples use broad matchers and verbatim audit logging that users should narrow before deployment.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact consists of Markdown documentation files only, with no executable files, install scripts, active frontmatter hooks, or automatic runtime behavior in the submitted package.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Examples include local file logging, project-file context injection, and outbound HTTP hook patterns; these are expected for a hook guide but should be limited to trusted files, trusted endpoints, and minimized payloads.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Persistent logs, cross-session state, durable scheduled tasks, and cleanup commands are discussed as examples, not automatically enabled; users should review retention, deletion, and permission implications before copying them.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install is reasonable if you want hook-authoring guidance, but treat the examples as templates to harden, not drop-in policy. Before enabling hooks based on this skill, narrow matchers, avoid raw audit logging, use trusted HTTPS endpoints only, redact sensitive fields, make persistence opt-in with retention controls, and review any destructive cleanup commands manually.
llm.findings:
[VirusTotal] expected: Telemetry was clean, with no malicious or suspicious engine detections; this supports but does not determine the benign verdict.
[staticScan] expected: The static scan reported no suspicious patterns, and local inspection found only Markdown documentation files.
[SQP-2] expected: HTTP hook and remote configuration examples disclose outbound hook data flows, but users should add their own trust-boundary controls because hook payloads may contain sensitive session or tool data.
[SQP-2] expected: Audit logging examples are purpose-aligned and sometimes include redaction guidance, but users should avoid logging raw tool inputs, prompts, outputs, secrets, or personal data.
[SQP-2] expected: Context injection and elicitation examples are relevant to hook authoring, but they can expose local project context or user-supplied form content if copied without consent and minimization.
[SQP-2] expected: The copy-pasteable cleanup command example uses a destructive rm -rf pattern for narrowly listed temporary paths; it is disclosed, but should be reviewed before execution.
[RA2] expected: The persistent-state example stores only counters under ~/.claude and is not automatically installed; persistence should remain opt-in, documented, and limited to non-sensitive data.
